title: Did a President Really Spend $200 on Ice Cream in One Summer?
summary: Imagine a scoop of ice cream taller than you! In 2014, workers in Wisconsin used 733 tubs of ice cream to build a giant scoop that weighed 3,010 pounds. That's heavier than a small car! But ice cream's story is even cooler than that. Did you know that the first ice-cream-like dessert was made in China over 1,000 years ago? It used milk, flour, and something called camphor (a waxy stuff from trees). Later, Arab chefs in the 9th century made a version with milk and sugar. Ice cream didn't come to America until 1744, when a governor served strawberry ice cream at a fancy party. Everyone loved it! George Washington, the first president, spent about $200 on ice cream in one summer. That was a huge amount of money back then! Thomas Jefferson even wrote his own vanilla ice cream recipe. But ice was hard to keep frozen, so only rich people could enjoy it. That changed in 1851 when the first ice cream factory opened in Pennsylvania. Now, Americans eat about 23 pounds of ice cream per person each year. That's like carrying around two big bags of flour! Some scientists think your favorite flavor says something about you. Vanilla fans might be adventurous, while chocolate lovers are often outgoing. Mint chocolate chip fans? Ambitious and confident. So, what's your scoop say about you?
why_it_matters: Learning about ice cream's past shows how a simple treat connects people across centuries and cultures, just like your own favorite dessert might have a story.

background_read: Before freezers existed, people in the 1700s stored ice from frozen lakes in special ice houses, so ice cream was a treat only for the very wealthy, like presidents.
George Washington (the first president of the United States) spent a large sum on ice cream, and Thomas Jefferson (the third U.S. president) wrote his own recipe for it.
When the first ice cream factory opened in Pennsylvania in 1851, the cold dessert finally became cheap enough for regular families to enjoy.
Article_Structure: WHO: Ancient Chinese chefs, Arab cooks, George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, and modern ice cream fans.
WHAT: The surprising journey of ice cream from a rare dessert in China over 1,000 years ago to a popular treat everyone enjoys today.
WHERE: China, the Middle East, and the United States.
WHY: To explore ice cream's long history and share the fun idea that your favorite flavor might reveal something about your personality.
